# `lunar-infrastructure`

Scenario kind of the engine v0.38.0, family [Lunar and cislunar](../lunar-and-cislunar.md). Advisory: analysis output from a research and engineering tool, not type-approved navigation equipment and not a safety-of-life service. Every label here is the engine's or the verification matrix's; a kind is MODELLED unless the matrix says otherwise (how a label is earned: the README's Evidence section).

## What it does

MODELLED studies of the Moon's orbit and surface as navigation and geodetic infrastructure, five studies behind one kind selected by `study`: od-consistency (onboard Earth-GNSS orbit determination in an NRHO or ELFO against independent ground radiometric orbit determination, judged by their own covariances over a seeded Monte Carlo), carrier-phase (joint surface-orbiter double-differenced carrier phase and integer ambiguity resolution with LAMBDA), frame-coestimation (a surface station and orbiters added to Earth-station ranging for the seven-parameter lunar frame datum), space-tie (GNSS, VLBI and laser ranging on one spacecraft, frame-tie precision against the local-tie error) and geodesy-sensitivity (Fisher information of the lunar Love numbers h2, k2, l2 and the physical libration from laser ranging, orbiter tracking, a surface gravimeter and a surface clock). A restricted three-body model with stated simplifications; the numerics are checked against independent programs and nothing is compared with a measurement of a lunar quantity.

One run of `scenarios/lunar-infrastructure-space-tie.toml` summarises as: lunar-infrastructure space-tie: 4 sweep points on 1 arcs; laser-vs-GNSS x translation sigma 1.0363 m at the registered local tie

## Evidence

No matrix row names this kind by name; the label on its result is the engine's own, above.

The rows the run itself exercised, with the oracle the matrix gives each (the public sources are named there):

- **MODELLED** Deterministic, scenario-hashed, SBOM + cross-platform golden gates. Oracle (ExternalDataset): SBOM conformance to the official CycloneDX 1.5 JSON Schema (+ valid SPDX identifiers) — an external published standard, zero validation errors over the full dependency graph; the FoM-determinism / byte-reproducibility part remains a pinned self-consistency check, so the row stays MODELLED
- **MODELLED** Orbit determination in a near-rectilinear halo orbit (or an elliptical frozen orbit) from two independent data types: Earth-GNSS pseudoranges received on board . Oracle (ReferenceImpl): An independent scipy/numpy program integrates the same variational equations (bar O1). Nothing is compared with a measurement of a lunar orbit. The oracle checks the numerics of stated formulas, not the physics, so the row stays MODELLED. Restricted three-body model: no Sun, no lunar harmonics, the Earth rotation axis along the orbit normal, ILLUSTRATIVE receiver and station inputs.
- **MODELLED** Between-receiver single-differenced Earth-GNSS carrier phase and code at a lunar surface station and an orbiter, with the per-epoch clock difference profiled ou. Oracle (ReferenceImpl): An independent numpy solve of the same normal equations from the exported rows (Q3) and a brute-force integer enumeration (Q4). No GNSS or lunar carrier-phase measurement is compared with. MODELLED.
- **MODELLED** Fisher information of the seven-parameter lunar frame datum from Earth-station laser ranging to the five reflectors alone and with orbiter-to-surface-station ra. Oracle (ReferenceImpl): An independent numpy finite difference of the forward model (F2). Nothing is compared with real lunar frame solutions. The factor is conditional on the assumed known orbit and the 1 m range sigma. MODELLED.
- **MODELLED** Cramer-Rao precision of the inter-technique translation, scale and rotation offsets between GNSS, VLBI and laser-ranging frames when one spacecraft carries all . Oracle (ReferenceImpl): An independent numpy stacked system with the position unknowns eliminated by explicit Schur complements (T3). No GRASP, Genesis or other mission data are compared with. MODELLED.
